texts.facts: The Detailed Accident Report (Dar) filed on 08.11.2016 was registered as a Motor Accident Claim petition. Separate Claim Petition was also filed by the petitioner. The DAR revealed that a Road Traffic Accident took place on 08.07.2016 at about 8.00 P.M. in front of outer Ring Road near ITI Dheerpur, Burari Chowk, Burari, Delhi, wherein the petitioner Pramod had sustained grievous injury. The accident took place with the vehicle i.e. Bus bearing registration No. DL-1P-C2246 driven by respondent no.1 Sh. Ebney Hassan, owned by respondent no.2 Rajeev Kumar. The said vehicle was insured with National Insurance Co. Ltd. BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE: 2. The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that on 08.07.2016, DD No.32A was received at P.S. Burari regarding an accident. That on 08.07.2016, the petitioner along with his colleague Sh. Subhash Chand was coming from Supreme Court, Bhagwan Dass Road, New Delhi towards his residence at Kamal Vihar, Kamalpur, Burari, Delhi by motorcycle bearing no. UP16-V-3706. The said motorcycle was being driven by Subhash Chand. When they reached in front of Outer Ring Road near ITI Dheerpur, Burari Chowk, Burari, Delhi at about 8:00 PM on 08.07.2016, the offending vehicle i.e. Bus bearing no. DL-1PCC-2246, driven by respondent no. 1, hit the said motorcycle with forceful impact from behind. It is further averred that the said bus was coming at a very high speed and was driven in the most rash and negligent manner without caring for the traffic rules and safety of passersby, due to which the petitioner and his colleague Subhash fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries. Both of them were taken to Jagjivan Ram Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi by PCR. There the MLC no. 129620/16 dated 08.07.2016 was prepared at the hospital and FIR no. 332/2016 was lodged on 09.07.2016 at PS Burari, Delhi u/s 279/338 IPC against the driver of the offending bus. It is averred that all the respondents are liable to compensate the petitioner for the injuries caused to him. 3. During the course of investigation, the IO prepared the site plan of the place of accident. The offending vehicle was sent for mechanical inspection. The IO deposited the MLC of the injured in the hospital for final opinion. He, later, collected the MLC of the injured after final opinion and the injury was shown as 'grievous' on the MLC of the petitioner, therefore, section 338 IPC was added. On completion of investigation, chargesheet under section 279/338 IPC was filed against the driver/respondent no. 1 Ebney Hassan and DAR was filed before this Tribunal on 08.11.2016. 4. Respondent nos. 1 and 2 did not file their written statement, therefore, their defence was struck off vide order dated 14.05.2018. Respondent no. 3 filed their legal offer but later disputed the identity of the offending vehicle and submitted that the offending vehicle was never involved in any accident. (OPP) 3. Relief. EVIDENCE 6. To prove its case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1; Sh. Shrii Bhagwan as PW-2; HC Jai Bhagwan as PW-3 and Dr. Dhanshree as PW-4. The respondents did not lead any evidence. 7. The Petitioner filed the Form XIV. Financial statement of the petitioner has been recoded. Final arguments were heard on behalf of the petitioner as well as respondent no. 3. FINDINGS & OBSERVATIONS 8. The factum of accident: 11. In this matter to prove the occurrence of the accident as well as the rashness and negligence on the part of the driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1, the petitioner (PW-1) in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A had deposed as under:- "... 2. That on 08.07.2016 I along with my colleague Sh. Subhash Chand were coming from Supreme Court, Bhagwan Dass Road, New Delhi towards our residence at Kamal Vihar, Kamalpur, Burari, Delhi by motorcycle bearing registration no. UP 16V 3706. Sh. Subhash Chand also resides in the nearby location at Kaushik Enclave, Burari, Delhi. 4. That I and my colleague Subhash both were removed to Babu Jagjivan Ram Memorial Hospital, Jahangir Puri, Delhi 33 by PCR where the concerned doctor(s) attended me and other injured. That the concerned police lodged FIR bearing no. 332/2016 dated 9.07.2016 in PS Burari District Central, Delhi under section 279/338 IPC of IPC against the driver i.e. respondent no. 1 of the offending Bus no. DL1PC2246 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle). Thereafter, the injured was again admitted in Actional Medical Institute on 03.11.2016 where he was diagnosed with "FTP acute on chronic SDH with mass effect." and a surgery was performed which was "left craniotomy with decompression of SDH onlay duroplasty fixation cranioplasty". He was discharged on 08.11.2016. The above medical bills have not been disputed by the respondents and therefore, the same stand proved. However, it is an admitted case on behalf of the petitioner that Rs. 17,827/- was reimbursed to him by his department as medical reimbursement. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to get the compensation for the bills mentioned in aforesaid Table No. 1 i.e. Rs. 1,26,129.15/- minus Rs. 17,827/- which equals to Rs. 1,08,302.15/- towards medical expenses. Loss of income: 28. Coming to the aspect of loss of income, the petitioner Pramod Kumar claimed that he was working in Delhi Police as Head Constable and has suffered loss of income to the tune of Rs. 18,477/-. However, he has not filed any document on record to prove the same. Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 17 The salary slips placed on record by the petitioner himself shows that his salary was Rs. 27,962/- in the month of July 2017 i.e. at the time of the accident. Even after the accident, the injured got a salary of Rs. 27,865/- in the month of September, 2017 and in November, 2019 it was Rs. 35,313/-. Thus, there seems to be no apparent loss of income and thus, no compensation is awarded under this head. Loss of earned leave: 29. The petitioner had claimed loss of 150 earned leaves which equals to five months of salary on the ground that due to the accident, he had to take leave for 150 days which were deducted from his earned leave. He also asserted that these 150 days of earned leave would have been encashed at the time of his retirement and he would have got salary equal to 150 days which he will not now. Thus, he has suffered a loss of salary for 150 days. He examined HC Jai Bhagwan as PW-3 who proved the sanction letter which was already Ex. PW-1/8 by virtue of which 150 earned leaves were sanctioned in favour of the injured for the medical case. Ex. PW-1/8 shows at serial no. 20 that the injured was granted 150 days of earned leave w.e.f. 09.07.2016 i.e. a day after his accident. The earned leaves is calculated on the basis of basic pay plus DA. The basic pay of the injured at the time of the accident i.e. on 08.07.2016 was Rs. 41,600/- and DA was Rs. 1,644/-. Thus, his total gross income at the time of the accident was Rs. 43, 244/- which would be considered for the earned leave. Thus, the injured would be entitled to loss of earned leave for five months i.e. Rs. 43,244/- x 5 = Rs. 2,16,220/-. Pain and Suffering: 30. The petitioner/ injured has claim Rs. 1,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering, however, no justification has been given for claiming this amount. It is true that a particular amount cannot be fixed under the head pain and suffering which could be applicable to all cases as it varies from case to case. Judicial notice can be taken of the fact that since the petitioner has received grievous injuries, therefore, petitioner must have suffered pain and sufferings owing to the said injuries. The petitioner/ injured has claim Rs. 1,00,000/- under the head mental shock but no justification has been given for claiming such a huge amount. Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 18 Special Diet: 32. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 2,31,000/- under the head special diet but there is no cogent evidence on record regarding money spent by the petitioner upon special diet. However, considering the nature of injuries suffered by the injured/petitioner, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner must have spent some money under this head. Hence, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of Rs. 5,000/- towards expenses incurred on special diet. Conveyance charges: 33. The petitioner has claimed Rs. 11,500/- under the head conveyance charges. He has also filed certain bills of the taxi which total to 3,832/-. Attendant charges: 34. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 45,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record for the money spent by the petitioner upon an attendant. Loss of amenities: 35. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 1,00,000/- under this head, however, there is no cogent evidence on record regarding any loss of amenity to the petitioner. Loss of earning inconvenience, hardships, disappointment, frustration, mental stress, dejectment and unhappiness in future life etc.: 36. The petitioner/ injured has claimed Rs. 1,50,000/- under this head. However, there is no proof or averment on record that the injured has suffered any loss of earning inconvenience, hardships, disappointment, frustration, mental stress, dejectment or unhappiness in future life. etc. Thus, no compensation is granted under this head. Future loss of income: Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 19 37. The petitioner Pramod Kumar has not claimed any loss of future income as he continues to serve in Delhi Police at the same pay level. (Loss of earned leave) Mental & Physical Shock & Pain & Rs. 20,000/- + Rs. 50,000/- = Suffering Rs. 70,000/- Special diet Rs. 5,000/- Attendant charges Rs. 5,000/- Conveyance charges Rs. 3,832/- Loss of amenities Rs. 5,000/- Disfiguration Nil. Loss of Marriage prospects Nil. Loss of earning, inconvenience, Nil. hardship, disappointment, frustration, mental stress, dejectment and unhappiness in future life etc. Total Rs. 4,41,316/- (rounded off to Rs. 4,41,316/-) 39. In the case of Benson George v Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd. in Civil Appeal No. 1540 of 2022 decided on 25.02.2022, Hon'ble Supreme Court had awarded an interest of 6% per annum. Therefore, it is held that the petitioner shall be entitled to interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of DAR i.e. 08.11.2016 till realization. DISBURSEMENT Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 20 40. The Financial Statement of the petitioner/injured was recorded by this Court/Tribunal. As per the said statement, the monthly expenses of his family are approximately Rs. 50,000/- per month. Total Rs. 4,41,316.15/- 1(i+ii+iii+iv+viii)+2(i+ii+iii) (rounded off to Rs. 4,41,316/-) 5. Total Compensation Rs. 4,41,316/- Interest awarded 6% 6. Earlier award amount (which has already been received by the petitioner in terms of previous award passed by Ld. - Predecessor) to be deducted 7. Interest amount upto the date of Rs. 1,94,914.56/- award (05 months) (rounded off to Rs. 1,94,915/-) 8. Total amount including Interest Rs. 6,36,231/- 9. Award amount released As mentioned in para no. 41 10. Award amount kept in FDRs As mentioned in para no. 41 11. Mode of disbursement of the As mentioned in para no. 41 award amount of the claimant(s) 12. Next date for compliance of the 17.04.2024 award LIABILITY: 44. The offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 Ebney Hassan, owned by respondent no. 2, Rajeev Kumar and insured with respondent no.3, National Insurance Co. Ltd. Thus, while respondent nos. 1 and 2 shall be jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount, respondent no. 3/ insurance company is liable to indemnify respondent nos. 1 and 2 for the award amount. RELIEF 45. Ahlmad is directed to e-mail an authenticated copy of the award to the insurance company for compliance within the time granted as directed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in WP (Civil) Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 23 No. 534/2020 titled as Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Union of India & Ors. on 16.03.2021. The said respondent is further directed to give intimation of deposit of the compensation amount to the claimant and shall file a compliance report with the Claims Tribunal with respect to the deposit of the compensation amount within 15 days of the deposit with a copy to the Claimant and his counsel. Ahlmad shall also e-mail an authenticated copy of the award to Branch Manager, SBI, Tis Hazari Courts for information.
texts.arguments: Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287). In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 3 Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion. In this regard, reliance is placed on the judgments of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the cases of Teja Singh Vs Suman & Ors., MAC. APP. 690/2017 & CM APPL. 28108/2017, titled as Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs Mona & Ors., date of decision 15.10.2019, which had relied upon the judgment in the case of Cholamandalam Insurance Co. Ltd. No convincing material has been brought on record by the respondents to show that no accident took place or that respondent no. 1 was not rash and negligent while driving the offending vehicle. 14. It is also settled law that the claimants cannot be expected to prove the accident to the hilt and the principle of res ipse loquitor should apply which means that the "accident speaks for itself". 15. Furthermore, in view of filing of DAR containing the charge-sheet for the offences u/s 279/338 IPC and other relevant documents against the respondent no. 1 and in terms of the judgment in the case of National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, respondent no. 1 Ebney Hassan (driver of the offending vehicle) is held to be negligent on the basis of preponderance of probability. Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in its guiding lamp post judgment for ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular injury cases. In the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Ors. (2011) 1 SCC 34, Hon'ble Supreme Court held as under: Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 7 "General principles relating to compensation in injury cases 4. The provision of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (`Act' for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The Court or tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. (See C. K. Subramonia Iyer vs. T. Kunhikuttan Nair - AIR 1970 SC 376, R. D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Ltd. - 1995 (1) SCC 551 and Baker vs. Willoughby - 1970 AC 467). 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following : Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be Pramod (I)(Fir332/16/Burari) vs Ebney Hassan (Nic) on 18 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149192690/ 8 granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. Assessment of pecuniary damages under item (i) and under item (ii)(a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation (see for example, the decisions of this court in Arvind Kumar Mishra vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - 2010(10) SCALE 298 and Yadava Kumar v. D.M., National Insurance Co. Ltd. - 2010 (8) SCALE 567). 9. An appropriate multiplier needs to be ascertained as per judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in matter of Sarla Verma Vs. DTC 2009 ACJ 1298 SC according to age of the injured/victim. Ld. Counsel for the petitioner had also argued that the petitioner has suffered heavy losses due to the accident and therefore, the entire amount be released to him.
